newsitem.title: FINLAND: ILKKA UP AS HEALTHY PROFITS BOOST DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: ILKKA UP AS HEALTHY PROFITS BOOST DEMAND.

text.p: Finnish newspaper and publishing house Ilkka Oy's share hit a new two-year high in moderate trade on Tuesday boosted by increased demand following strong January-August earnings released in October, brokers said.
At 1605/1405 GMT, Ilkka's more liquid II-series share traded at 161.00 markka, up 3.00 markka or almost two percent, after hitting 165.00 markka -- its highest since November 10, 1994.
Trade was about one million markka, which is quite active for Ilkka.
"Ilkka is rising as it has been cheap compared to some other stocks in the sector," one broker said, referring to another big listed media group Aamulehti-yhtyma Oy .
Aamulehti's II-share was up 2.00 markka at 142.00, which is about 12 times the company's 1995 earnings. At 161.00 markka, Ilkka was trading at 6.2 times its 1995 earnings.
On October 22, Ilkka released its eight-month report, which showed a 24.3 million markka profit before extraordinary items and taxes, up from 23.6 million markka in January-August 1995.
